static_traits.name: He Lin
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; no psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, fairly cooperative; rather negative tone, self-demanding; skeptical about Intervention but willing to try

basic_info.main_problem: When unable to clear challenging levels in games, I develop negative thoughts about my gaming ability, feeling incompetent and self-critical, affecting my mood and enjoyment of games.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to reduce game-performance-related negative thoughts through counseling, ease Low mood and self-criticism, Recovery interest in and enjoyment of games.
growth_experiences: Several months ago after encountering a particularly difficult level in a beloved game, began frequently having 'I am a bad player' negative thoughts; since then, whenever encountering harder parts in games, similar Self-denial is triggered. As seeing other players' successes online and comparing, the problem further worsened; tried coping through breaks, watching tutorials, and seeking online tips, but negative thoughts keep recurring, turning the gaming experience from relaxing and pleasant to tense and Depressed.

special_situations.event: Being unable to clear difficult levels or facing high-difficulty segments in games
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot easily clear high-difficulty levels, it means my ability is insufficient, I am a bad player
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated practice, temporary rest, watching tutorials, and looking for online tips, but often avoiding more detailed tutorials or others' help because of the notion that 'I should figure it out myself'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just not good / I am a bad player

special_situations.event: Sees other players clearing levels or performing at a high level online and compares
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot keep up with them or fall behind in progress, it proves I am not good enough and do not deserve to be called a player
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently checking others' records and achievements, reducing discussions of my Self-doubt with friends to avoid embarrassment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all better than me; I can never catch up with them

special_situations.event: Each time preparing to try or currently tackling a difficult part of a game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot do it now, I will never do it well in the future; failure means I am beyond help
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stepping back briefly to rest, repeatedly using familiar strategies while unwilling to try new approaches
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it this time; there is no hope afterwards either

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a capable, respect-worthy player and gain pleasure from it
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being dismissed, appearing inferior to others in comparison, experiencing shame and failure
defense_goal: Controls disappointment and shame through self-criticism and high standards
Avoiding exposing vulnerability to others to reduce the risk of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough failure, a 'lousy player' who could be exposed at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking of asking online friends for help or watching more detailed tutorials
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Asking for help equals admitting I cannot do it, and I will be seen as not good enough
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use self-demanding statements with 'should/must' (e.g. 'I should handle it myself'), in a rigid tone, avoiding asking for help directly and instead emphasizing self-reliance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes behavioral experiments or improvement suggestions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Even with effort I might still fail; these attempts may not necessarily be useful
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Listing reasons for potential failure in a calm but skeptical tone (such as 'what if I still fail'), lowering emotional investment, but on the surface still agreeing to try.

manifestations: Games originally meant for relaxation and enjoyment have become tense and painful due to repeated Self-denial
Experiences intense frustration around difficult levels, with enjoyment markedly reduced
outcomes: Low mood and self-criticism have increased
Waning interest in and enjoyment of games

manifestations: Although there are online gaming friends to talk to, embarrassment keeps me from bringing up Self-doubt
Feeling alienated from others in comparisons
outcomes: Social support not yet effectively used; the distress continues

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' self-demands (e.g. 'I should handle it myself')
Treats 'only solo completion counts as a good player' as an absolute rule, resisting asking others for help

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: In counseling, is clearly skeptical of behavioral experiments and blames oneself
Reinforcing Self-denial after comparing with others, expressing vulnerability and seeking help less

positive_force: Having the willingness to practice and learn, willing to try different strategies (e.g. watching tutorials, finding techniques)
Has certain online friend resources that can provide potential support
Able to notice negative thinking and willing to seek help for change
negative_force: Self-demanding, defining value by high standards ('should pass easily')
Self-labeling and a sense of despair after comparing with others
Predicting failure; an overgeneralizing maladaptive thinking pattern
Avoiding asking for help out of shame; insufficient use of social support

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and catastrophizing appear when frustrated in a game (such as 'I am a bad player')
antecedent: Facing difficult levels or high-difficulty sections
Watches others' high-level game completions and scores and compares
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating one failure with overall inadequacy, internalizing the rigid rule of 'should clear levels easily'; highly sensitive to others' evaluations and comparisons
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the experience of failure and shame, lowering investment and expectations through preemptive dismissal; finding an explanation for continued frustration to seek short-term psychological relief
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and sense of frustration intensified, gaming enjoyment decreased, practice efficiency and willingness to learn new strategies reduced

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding asking others for help or learning in depth (avoiding watching more detailed tutorials, avoiding discussing Self-doubt with friends)
antecedent: When thinking of seeking help or using more systematic tutorials
Worrying in social situations about being seen as not skilled enough
target_behavior.core_reason: Having internalized the rule of 'should rely on myself', worrying that showing vulnerability will be judged as not good enough
target_behavior.function: Maintains self-image, reduces the risk of being judged, lowers shame in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient use of resources, limited skill improvement, problems persisting and reinforcing Self-denial
